tasks.title: Extend Core Interface Substrate
tasks.context: Implement the load-bearing shared adapter substrate required by .metis/strategies/NULL/initiatives/RIT-I-0006/initiative.md REQ-501 in packages/core. Existing ground truth is packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/response.py, which already defines InterfaceResponse, Question, and ProvenanceRef, and packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/errors.py, which already defines ErrorCode, WarningCode, CoreError, CoreWarning, and ResumeKitError. Extend this substrate with stable interface result mapping helpers, a provider-not-configured error code, and an exit-code map that every transport will reuse; do not add Typer, MCP, FastAPI, uvicorn, or httpx to core.
acceptance_criteria: Core exposes a single result-shaping substrate over InterfaceResponse so callers can build success, failure, provider-not-configured, human-input-required, and exception-mapped responses without inventing transport-local envelopes.
ErrorCode contains a stable provider-not-configured code distinct from generic provider unavailable errors, and tests assert its serialized value is stable.

A deterministic exit-code mapping exists for ok, invalid input/validation failure, provider not configured/provider unavailable, human input required, and internal/unknown errors; warnings alone do not produce a non-zero exit code.
Mapping helpers preserve warnings, errors, requires_human_input, questions, provenance, and artifacts separately in the InterfaceResponse envelope.

Unit tests cover success mapping, strict warning handling if supported by the helper, provider-not-configured mapping, ResumeKitError mapping, generic exception mapping, human-input mapping, and exit-code selection.
No heavy interface dependency is added to packages/core/pyproject.toml or imported from any core source file.
tasks.implementation_notes: Prefer a new packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/interface.py for mapping helpers and exit-code constants so response.py and errors.py remain small; edit errors.py only for the new ErrorCode value. Use existing InterfaceResponse.success, InterfaceResponse.failure, InterfaceResponse.needs_input, CoreError, CoreWarning, ErrorCode, ResumeKitError, ArtifactRef, ProvenanceRef, and Question. Leave packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/__init__.py exports to the late public-export task unless tests need submodule imports. Keep all code provider- and transport-agnostic.

tasks.title: Build Capability Facade Package
tasks.context: Create the single in-process capability facade that all transports call. The facade cannot live in packages/core without creating dependency cycles because existing engine packages depend on resume-kit-core, so place it in a small dedicated workspace package packages/facade exposing resume_kit_facade. It must wrap exactly these engine public APIs: resume_kit_document_parser.parse_resume_structured and extract_resume_text_only, resume_kit_job_parser.parse_job_description and parse_job_description_text_only, resume_kit_ats.compute_ats_score, resume_kit_matching.check_job_match, select_best, compare_versions, and analyze_keyword_gaps, resume_kit_alignment.align_resume, and resume_kit_evidence.validate_resume_truth and build_candidate_evidence. Every callable returns resume_kit_core.InterfaceResponse via the core substrate from Extend Core Interface Substrate.
acceptance_criteria: packages/facade is a typed Hatchling workspace package named resume-kit-facade with import package resume_kit_facade, py.typed, README, and package-local tests; uv sync can resolve it from the packages/* workspace wildcard.

The facade provides one uniform callable per exposed capability: extract-resume, extract-job-description, check-resume-ats, check-resume-job-match, select-best-resume, compare-resume-versions, identify-resume-gaps, align-resume, validate-resume-truth, and build-candidate-evidence.

Facade request/config models are transport-agnostic and typed with resume_kit_schemas models such as ResumeDocument, JobDescription, AlignmentResult, TruthReport, ATSScore, JobMatchReport, KeywordGapAnalysis, ResumeSelectionResult, ResumeComparisonResult, and CandidateEvidence.

No-LLM deterministic mode works for extract-resume via extract_resume_text_only, extract-job-description via parse_job_description_text_only, ATS/matching/select/compare/gaps/truth/evidence via deterministic engine calls, and align-resume via an explicit deterministic no-change path only when no_llm is true.
LLM-requiring calls made without a StructuredCompletionProvider return the stable provider-not-configured InterfaceResponse error from the core substrate instead of calling the engine or crashing.

align-resume correctly awaits the async resume_kit_alignment.align_resume engine function; tests use FakeStructuredCompletionProvider from packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/testing.py for provider paths.
Facade tests assert that the facade is the only place transport tasks need to call engine functions directly and that no transport dependency is imported by resume_kit_facade.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use a new package rather than core because core already sits below document-parser, job-parser, ats, matching, evidence, and alignment in the dependency graph. Suggested files are models.py for request/options models and capabilities.py for individual functions plus a stable capability registry. For check-resume-ats, compute KeywordGapAnalysis with analyze_keyword_gaps(job, resume, resume), pass gap.current_match_percentage, gap.non_injectable_keywords, and gap.injectable_keywords into compute_ats_score. Keep provider construction out of the facade; accept provider: StructuredCompletionProvider | None. Do not expose deferred Phase 6 capabilities or stubs.

tasks.title: Scaffold Interface Packages
tasks.context: Scaffold the three transport workspace packages required by RIT-I-0006 plus their isolated dependencies: packages/cli exposing resume_kit_cli, packages/mcp exposing resume_kit_mcp, and packages/api exposing resume_kit_api. Follow packages/matching/pyproject.toml and packages/ats/pyproject.toml for Hatchling, [tool.uv.sources], src/<import_name>/py.typed, README, and package-local tests conventions. Hyphenated package directories must not contain tests/__init__.py because root pyproject.toml uses pytest --import-mode=importlib.
acceptance_criteria: packages/cli, packages/mcp, and packages/api each contain pyproject.toml, README.md, src/<import_name>/__init__.py, src/<import_name>/py.typed, and a minimal importable module stub for the future implementation.
packages/cli is named resume-kit-cli, depends on resume-kit-facade plus only its CLI transport dependency Typer, and declares [project.scripts] resume-tool pointing at the Typer app entry point.
packages/mcp is named resume-kit-mcp, depends on resume-kit-facade plus only the official mcp Python SDK for MCP transport behavior.

packages/api is named resume-kit-api, depends on resume-kit-facade plus only FastAPI and uvicorn for runtime, with httpx/TestClient support isolated to package test dependencies or dependency groups rather than engine packages.
uv sync --all-packages resolves all new workspace packages and their workspace sources.
No engine package pyproject.toml gains Typer, click, mcp, FastAPI, uvicorn, httpx, or any transport dependency.
tasks.implementation_notes: This is scaffold only. Keep app/server/routes stubs minimal so later CLI, MCP, and API implementation tasks own behavior in their package files. Do not touch root pyproject.toml unless uv workspace resolution proves it necessary; the existing members = ["packages/*"] wildcard should pick up these packages. uv.lock is claimed here because adding package dependencies will update the lockfile.
verification_steps: uv run python -c "import resume_kit_cli, resume_kit_mcp, resume_kit_api"

tasks.title: Implement Resume Tool CLI
tasks.context: Implement packages/cli as a thin Typer adapter over resume_kit_facade. The CLI command names from RIT-I-0006 are extract, extract-job, check-ats, match, select, compare, identify-gaps, align, validate-truth, and build-evidence, corresponding to the 10 facade capabilities. The package must install the resume-tool entry point from packages/cli/pyproject.toml and must never call engine packages directly; all work goes through resume_kit_facade and returns or formats resume_kit_core.InterfaceResponse.
acceptance_criteria: resume-tool exposes exactly the 10 Phase 5 commands and no deferred Phase 6 commands or stubs.

Every command supports --output {json,text,md}, --no-llm where applicable, --strict, --human-in-loop/--non-interactive where applicable, --evidence <path> where applicable, and --config <path> without persisting configuration or resume/job content.

Commands read file/JSON inputs into facade request models, call only resume_kit_facade capability functions, and render the returned InterfaceResponse without redefining response, warning, error, provenance, artifact, or question shapes.

Exit status comes exclusively from the core exit-code map; requires_human_input uses the reserved human-input exit code, provider-not-configured uses the provider error exit code, and warnings alone remain success unless --strict intentionally maps them through the shared substrate.
No-LLM deterministic contract tests pass for text extraction, job text parsing, ATS, job match, select, compare, gaps, truth validation, and evidence building with no provider and no network.
Provider-requiring paths without configured provider return the structured provider-not-configured error in JSON output and never raise a traceback in normal usage.
Typer CliRunner tests cover command registration, JSON/text/Markdown output, strict mode, human-in-loop surfacing for align, and representative success/error exit codes.
tasks.implementation_notes: Keep parsing and formatting helpers inside packages/cli only, for example io.py and formatters.py, but do not put business rules there. Use ResumeDocument.model_validate_json/model_validate and JobDescription.model_validate_json/model_validate for JSON inputs. For align, wrap the facade async path with asyncio.run if the facade exposes async functions. Do not construct a real LLM provider in Phase 5; tests should use facade seams or FakeStructuredCompletionProvider only.

tasks.title: Implement MCP Tool Server
tasks.context: Implement packages/mcp as a thin official MCP Python SDK server over resume_kit_facade. RIT-I-0006 requires these stable MCP tool names: resume_extract, job_description_extract, resume_check_ats, resume_check_job_match, resume_select_best, resume_compare_versions, resume_identify_gaps, resume_align, resume_validate_truth, and candidate_evidence_build. The server must return structured JSON InterfaceResponse payloads with warnings separate from errors, requiresHumanInput/questions surfaced structurally, and provenance/artifacts preserved.
acceptance_criteria: The MCP server registers exactly the 10 stable tool names from the initiative and no unbuilt Phase 6 capabilities.

Each tool validates input into transport-agnostic facade request models, calls only resume_kit_facade, and returns InterfaceResponse.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True if aliases are introduced) or an equivalent stable JSON dict.
Tool outputs preserve data, warnings, errors, requires_human_input/requiresHumanInput, questions, provenance, and artifacts without MCP-local result-shape definitions.
No-LLM deterministic tool tests pass without any network, server socket, or concrete LLM provider.
Provider-requiring tool calls without a configured StructuredCompletionProvider return the facade/core provider-not-configured structured error.
align tool handling awaits the async facade/engine path and tests cover human-in-loop requires_human_input output without advancing review state.
MCP tests call handlers directly or through an in-memory MCP SDK session; they do not open a network port.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use the official mcp package from packages/mcp/pyproject.toml. Keep a direct handler registry in tools.py so tests can call handlers without stdio/network. server.py should build and expose the SDK server object. If the SDK uses decorators, keep the decorated functions as thin wrappers over the handler registry. Do not import Typer, FastAPI, uvicorn, or CLI/API code.

tasks.title: Implement FastAPI Routes
tasks.context: Implement packages/api as a thin FastAPI adapter over resume_kit_facade. RIT-I-0006 REQ-504 requires one REST endpoint per exposed capability, reusing resume_kit_schemas domain models and surfacing InterfaceResponse with warnings, errors, requires_human_input, questions, provenance, and artifacts. Endpoints should cover extract-resume, extract-job-description, check-resume-ats, check-resume-job-match, select-best-resume, compare-resume-versions, identify-resume-gaps, align-resume, validate-resume-truth, and build-candidate-evidence.
acceptance_criteria: resume_kit_api exposes a FastAPI app object with exactly one route per Phase 5 capability and no deferred Phase 6 routes.
Routes validate request bodies into facade request models and call only resume_kit_facade; no route imports document-parser, job-parser, ats, matching, evidence, or alignment directly.
Responses use the canonical InterfaceResponse structure and do not collapse warnings into errors or questions into plain strings.
No-LLM deterministic route tests pass using FastAPI TestClient/httpx in-process with no network and no LLM.

Provider-requiring route calls without a configured provider return a structured provider-not-configured InterfaceResponse error and an appropriate deterministic HTTP status policy documented in tests.
align-resume handles the async engine path correctly from FastAPI and surfaces human-in-loop requires_human_input/questions without running an interactive loop.
No persistence, auth, async job queue, retention, logging of resume/job content, or provider SDK integration is added.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use app.py for create_app/app construction, routes.py for route registration, and models.py only for transport request wrappers that are not already covered by facade models. Prefer returning InterfaceResponse models/dicts directly so FastAPI handles JSON encoding. Keep uvicorn only as package dependency/optional run target; tests should use TestClient. Do not import Typer or mcp.

tasks.title: Implement Job Hunter Bridge
tasks.context: Implement integrations/job-hunter as the typed library bridge required by RIT-I-0006 REQ-506. This bridge is not a transport server and must not mutate job-hunter state; it simply offers stable Python callables that job-hunter can import to analyze a resume for a job, align a resume for a job, validate truth, and build candidate evidence by delegating to resume_kit_facade and returning canonical InterfaceResponse payloads with resume_kit_schemas data.
acceptance_criteria: integrations/job-hunter contains a typed import package, py.typed marker, minimal pyproject.toml or equivalent local typing configuration, README, and tests.

Bridge functions include analyze_resume_for_job, align_resume_for_job, validate_truth, and build_evidence or equivalently named stable callables documented in README; each returns InterfaceResponse containing canonical schema data rather than bridge-local DTOs.
The bridge delegates to resume_kit_facade for check-resume-ats, check-resume-job-match, identify-resume-gaps, align-resume, validate-resume-truth, and build-candidate-evidence as appropriate.
The bridge never imports or writes job-hunter application state, storage, queues, HTTP clients, CLIs, MCP, FastAPI, or Typer.
No-LLM deterministic bridge tests pass without network or provider configuration.
Provider-requiring align behavior without provider returns the same structured provider-not-configured error unless no_llm is explicitly requested.
Tests assert input objects are not mutated and artifact/question/provenance fields are preserved in returned InterfaceResponse values.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use integrations/job-hunter/src/resume_kit_job_hunter_bridge/ as the import package to avoid hyphenated import names. Because root workspace membership is packages/*, verify with PYTHONPATH=integrations/job-hunter/src unless the implementer intentionally adds this integration to the workspace in a serialized scaffold change. Keep it pure library code over facade request models and options.
verification_steps: PYTHONPATH=integrations/job-hunter/src uv run mypy integrations/job-hunter/src integrations/job-hunter/tests

tasks.title: Author Resume Intelligence Skills
tasks.context: Create the markdown agent skills under plugins/resume-intelligence required by RIT-I-0006 REQ-505. The repo currently has no plugin skill files under plugins/ or integrations/ to mirror, so infer a clean Codex-style SKILL.md format from the installed skill convention: front matter with name and description, then concise operational instructions. Skills should tell an agent how to invoke the CLI resume-tool commands or the stable MCP tools, not reimplement resume intelligence logic in markdown.
acceptance_criteria: plugins/resume-intelligence contains markdown skill definitions covering exactly the 10 exposed Phase 5 capabilities and no deferred Phase 6 capabilities.

Each skill names the corresponding CLI command and MCP tool: extract/resume_extract, extract-job/job_description_extract, check-ats/resume_check_ats, match/resume_check_job_match, select/resume_select_best, compare/resume_compare_versions, identify-gaps/resume_identify_gaps, align/resume_align, validate-truth/resume_validate_truth, and build-evidence/candidate_evidence_build.
Skill instructions emphasize that interfaces are thin adapters over the engine/facade and that agents must not invent facts, bypass evidence, or create business rules in prompt text.
Skills document no-LLM deterministic usage and the expected provider-not-configured structured error for LLM-requiring paths without a configured provider.
A lightweight structure test verifies every SKILL.md has front matter, a description, references to either resume-tool or the stable MCP tool name, and no mention of unbuilt Phase 6 capabilities.
No runtime dependency, Python package, provider SDK, network behavior, or generated resume content is added under plugins/resume-intelligence.
tasks.implementation_notes: A coherent grouping is acceptable, but one skill directory per capability under plugins/resume-intelligence/skills/<capability>/SKILL.md is easiest to lint and mirrors installed skill layout. Include a top-level README.md for capability mapping. Keep markdown procedural and short: inputs, preferred deterministic mode when applicable, CLI/MCP invocation shape, expected InterfaceResponse fields, and safety notes.

tasks.title: Add Cross Surface Parity Tests
tasks.context: Add late parity tests for RIT-I-0006 REQ-508 after CLI, MCP, and API implementations exist. The goal is to prove that CLI, MCP, API, and the direct resume_kit_facade call all expose equivalent core data for the same deterministic inputs. Use Typer CliRunner for CLI, direct handler or in-memory MCP session for MCP, FastAPI TestClient for API, and no network or LLM.
acceptance_criteria: Parity tests exercise representative deterministic inputs through direct facade, CLI, MCP, and API for check-resume-job-match, check-resume-ats, identify-resume-gaps, validate-resume-truth, and build-candidate-evidence at minimum.
Parity tests include extract-job-description and extract-resume no-LLM paths where fixture shape makes deterministic comparison stable.
For each tested capability, data payloads are equivalent after normalizing transport serialization differences, and warnings/errors/requires_human_input remain semantically equivalent.
Provider-not-configured parity is asserted across CLI, MCP, and API for at least one LLM-requiring path invoked without --no-llm/provider.
Human-in-loop align parity asserts each surface returns requires_human_input/questions rather than advancing an interactive loop.
Tests are in-process only: CliRunner, MCP direct handler/in-memory session, and FastAPI TestClient; no server ports, provider SDKs, or network calls.
tasks.implementation_notes: Create local fixtures inside the parity test file or a private helper in tests/interface if needed, but avoid shared package code. Normalize InterfaceResponse JSON by loading into dicts and comparing data/errors/warnings/questions/provenance fields rather than comparing raw stdout or HTTP response objects. Do not change transport implementation files in this task unless a parity bug is found; if fixes are needed, coordinate serially with the relevant surface owner.

tasks.title: Add Interface Boundary Tests
tasks.context: Add the late architecture and dependency-boundary tests required by RIT-I-0006 NFR-502 and NFR-503. Existing tests/boundary/test_boundary_no_upstream_imports.py currently treats fastapi as forbidden across all packages and has a fixed known package set; update it carefully now that packages/facade, packages/cli, packages/mcp, and packages/api are intentional Phase 5 packages. The boundary must enforce engine packages import no interface package, and engine packages contain none of Typer/click, mcp, FastAPI, uvicorn, or httpx dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: The known packages boundary includes core, schemas, document-parser, matching, ats, job-parser, policy, evidence, alignment, facade, cli, mcp, and api.

Boundary tests allow FastAPI only in packages/api, Typer/click only in packages/cli, and mcp only in packages/mcp; these heavy deps remain forbidden in schemas, core, document-parser, job-parser, ats, matching, policy, evidence, alignment, and facade source files.
Engine source files do not import resume_kit_cli, resume_kit_mcp, resume_kit_api, resume_kit_facade, or resume_kit_job_hunter_bridge.
Engine pyproject.toml files do not declare typer, click, mcp, fastapi, uvicorn, httpx, starlette, or requests as dependencies.
Interface packages may import facade/core/schemas as needed, but facade does not import CLI, MCP, API, plugin, or job-hunter bridge code.
The tests continue to forbid upstream app.*, litellm, openai, anthropic, sqlalchemy, and persistence/web framework leaks where inappropriate.
Full boundary test suite passes without requiring network or importing upstream.
tasks.implementation_notes: Prefer adding a new tests/boundary/test_interface_boundaries.py and minimally editing tests/boundary/test_boundary_no_upstream_imports.py for the known package set and per-package transport allowances. Scan files as text like existing boundary tests to avoid import side effects. Include integrations/job-hunter/src in the facade/no-transport direction checks where relevant, but do not require integrations to be a workspace package.

tasks.title: Wire Public Interface Exports
tasks.context: Finish public API wiring after the substrate, facade, transports, bridge, and plugin files exist. Existing package roots such as packages/core/src/resume_kit_core/__init__.py export stable symbols, and Phase 5 should follow that pattern for new public entry points without forcing implementation tasks to fight over __init__.py files. This task exports the shared interface substrate, facade callables/models, transport app/server objects, and job-hunter bridge callables, plus public export smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: resume_kit_core exports the new interface mapping helpers, exit-code map/type, and provider-not-configured helpers added by Extend Core Interface Substrate without dropping existing exports such as InterfaceResponse, Question, StructuredCompletionProvider, and FakeStructuredCompletionProvider compatibility.
resume_kit_facade package root exports the 10 facade capability callables, request/options models, and capability registry intended for transports.
resume_kit_cli package root exports the Typer app and main entry point used by resume-tool.
resume_kit_mcp package root exports the MCP server factory/object and direct handler registry intended for tests/in-process use.
resume_kit_api package root exports create_app and app.
resume_kit_job_hunter_bridge exports analyze_resume_for_job, align_resume_for_job, validate_truth, and build_evidence or the final stable bridge names.
Public export tests import all intended symbols from package roots and assert no unbuilt Phase 6 capability is exported.
Final interface-local mypy and pytest commands pass after exports are wired.
tasks.implementation_notes: This is intentionally late because every package scaffold creates __init__.py but behavior lands in separate module tasks. Keep __all__ explicit and stable, following existing package root style. Do not add business logic in __init__.py files. If a transport module chose slightly different stable function names, export those names and update the tests in this task, but do not rename CLI commands or MCP tool names from the initiative.
verification_steps: uv run mypy packages/core packages/facade packages/cli packages/mcp packages/api
PYTHONPATH=integrations/job-hunter/src uv run mypy integrations/job-hunter/src integrations/job-hunter/tests

uv run pytest packages/core/tests/test_init_exports.py packages/facade/tests/test_public_exports.py packages/cli/tests/test_public_exports.py packages/mcp/tests/test_public_exports.py packages/api/tests/test_public_exports.py integrations/job-hunter/tests/test_public_exports.py
